subject: Re: Order schedule concession matrix — legal footnotes and Exhibit B
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@stratushealth.com>

Cc: procure@stratushealth.com
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing exhibit — marked Exhibit B and proposed concession matrix

Jonas,

Attached is our marked-up Exhibit B (pricing schedule) and a short note from procurement summarizing the ask. High level: Stratus needs clearer floor/cap behavior for seasonal spikes and a minimal true‑up window that limits retroactive credits.

Key asks:  
- A hard quarterly cap (not a rolling cap) for first 12 months to limit billing volatility.
- True‑up only once per quarter, with a 45‑day invoice mapping window.
- Clarify how exceeded token usage maps to the monthly invoice (we need a worked example).
- Any concession language should include an explicit clawback schedule for credits tied to commits.

We attached the annotated Exhibit B (Stratus_ExhibitB_marked.pdf) and the latest OrderForm_v3.docx. Please confirm receipt and let us know if Redwood can provide a one‑page concession matrix that maps commit tiers -> discounts -> clawback percentages.

Elena Ruiz
VP, Procurement
Stratus Health

Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit — marked Exhibit B and proposed concession matrix

Elena — thanks for the clear notes and the annotated Exhibit B. Got both attachments.

Quick read: we can do a fixed quarterly cap for the first year but need to align on how burst credits and overage pricing interact with Reserved Commit tiers. Laura (legal) & Markus (rev ops) are looped in to propose concrete wording and a short concession matrix.

Proposed next steps:  
1) Laura: can you draft a redline of Exhibit B with two options — (A) Quarterly hard cap with monthly smoothing; (B) Quarterly soft cap + reactive credit tranche.
2) Markus: please model a worked invoice mapping example for the quarter (assume 3-tier commit: 100k/300k/750k token tiers).
3) I will share the concession matrix we typically use internally and push for a single‑page table the counterparty can sign off quickly.

Elena — I'll aim to get a first pass back by Tue COB PT. If Stratus can tolerate a very narrow EMEA-style rollback window (30 days) for initial commit miscounts we might preserve revenue recognition consistency. If not, we'll prioritize the hard-cap variant.

Jonas Weber

Jonas / Markus / Elena — attaching a draft concession matrix (concession_matrix_redwood_v1.xlsx) and an annotated Exhibit B redline (high level comments in the footer).

Notes on legal treatment (summary):
- "Quarterly hard cap" option (Option A) language: add a discrete definition section in Exhibit B: "Quarterly Billing Cap": the aggregate billable units for an invoice period shall not exceed the Cap for that quarter; Cap resets at the start of each fiscal quarter. Provide an explicit mapping table in Annex 1.
- "Soft cap" option (Option B): retain per-token billing, but provide a discretionary credit pool that Redwood may apply post-invoice to smooth billing; define a simple clawback schedule (0–6 months) for incorrectly applied credits.
- True-up / invoice mapping: propose 45 days after quarter end for the supplier invoice + 30 days to dispute; any undisputed variances will flow into next invoice as described in Annex 2. 
- Clawback schedule: 25% credit reversal month 1, 50% month 2, 25% month 3. (We can alter percentages but keep a hard schedule.)

I recommend we avoid open-ended "reserve" language that allows perpetual backward adjustment. Draft paragraph suggestion included in the redline and a one-page concession matrix for sign-off. If Stratus insists on a hard quarterly cap that removes smoothing entirely, Revenue Ops must be able to reconcile monthly burst usage to reserved commits — Markus, please confirm operational feasibility.

Laura Bennett
Associate General Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachment(s): concession_matrix_redwood_v1.xlsx

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@stratushealth.com>

Laura — thanks for the thorough options. A few quick points from procurement after internal review: 

1) We appreciate Option B but it does not meet our auditors' requirement for predictability. For Q1 we must have a hard cap to present to our CFO.
2) The clawback schedule is OK in principle, but we need the ability to lock credits to specific invoice line items — not an aggregated pool.
3) The true‑up timing you propose (45 days + 30 days dispute) is close but we'd prefer a 60‑day absolute window for dispute on our side.

Forwarded for context (partial quote):

On Thu, 04 Mar 2027 at 09:18 Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@stratushealth.com> wrote:
> Attached is our marked-up Exhibit B (pricing schedule) and a short note from procurement summarizing the ask.

We will not accept any language that allows Redwood to retroactively change committed tiers beyond the 12‑month stabilization period. Please produce a worked invoice example (line by line) that maps an overage in March to a Q1 settlement under the hard-cap model.

Elena Ruiz
VP, Procurement
Stratus Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit — marked Exhibit B and proposed concession matrix

Elena — thanks for the clarity. Here's a proposed compromise that should meet Stratus's CFO needs while keeping revenue ops workable: 

- Hard quarterly cap for first 12 months (Cap defined per Exhibit B and resets each quarter).
- Within-quarter bursts are billed at overage rates but cannot push the charged amount above the quarter Cap; if overage charges would exceed the Cap, Redwood will credit the invoice up to the Cap and the excess usage will be treated as "overflow" and carried into a non-billable reconciliation bucket for internal tracking.
- True‑up timing: Redwood accepts a 60‑day dispute window (from quarter end) as requested. Any undisputed variances will be invoiced in the next billing period.
- Credits tied to commits will be applied to the exact invoice line item; clawback schedule will be 30/50/20 months 1/2/3 for adjustments (slightly frontloaded to preserve accounting).

Action items: 
- Laura: please prepare Exhibit B redline reflecting the Cap definition + Annex 1 (invoice mapping example) and Annex 2 (clawback schedule).
- Markus: produce the worked invoice example (three scenarios: under-commit, within tier, burst beyond cap) and confirm that Revenue Ops can implement the non-billable overflow tracking.
- Elena: once you confirm the table below (I pasted the short concession table we use) we'll circulate a final OrderForm_v4 for signature.

Concession Table (example — to be inserted into Exhibit B as Annex 3):
Tier | Commit (tokens/qtr) | Discount | Clawback %
Tier 1 | 100,000 | 0% | 0%
Tier 2 | 300,000 | 8% | 30%
Tier 3 | 750,000 | 16% | 50%

Elena — if that aligns I will ask Legal to get the redline to you by Mon COB PT and RevOps will drop the invoice mapping examples into HubSpot. Also sending DocuSign envelope when OrderForm_v4 is ready (DocuSign: envelope-0f4b9b2a).
